concept.title: Character styles or inline formatting
concept.abstract: This section covers Character Styles in Markdown — the inline formatting attributes that assign semantic meaning to individual words or phrases within a paragraph — and five scenarios: bold for general emphasis, bold for a UI element inside a procedure, monospace for inline code, monospace for a file path, and bold for a menu navigation sequence. The converter reads each named character style or font family to determine the appropriate DITA inline element; where named styles are absent, content pattern recognition refines the mapping.

conbody.p:
The Character styles are inline formatting attributes applied to individual words or phrases within a paragraph. For example,
A menu path or button label is bold to identify UI screen text as a named interface element.
A file path or command is monospace to identify it as executable or navigable content.

Marking these distinctions visually — bold, italic, or monospace — communicates meaning to readers. Translation memory tools, conditional processing engines, content reuse frameworks, and accessibility processors all require typed markup to treat each kind of text correctly in publishing systems.

In a Markdown file, character styles are applied through the following mechanisms:
Italics character style is applied through single asterisks or underscores such as *text* or _text_.
Bold character style is applied through double asterisks or underscores such as **text** or __text__.
Monospace character style is applied through single backticks such as `text`.
conbody.note: The DITA-XML converter reads each character styling to determine the appropriate DITA inline element.
conbody.p: When named styles are absent, the DITA-XML converter uses content pattern recognition to evaluate programming domain, UI domain, and software domain to refine the mappings. For example, a monospace run containing a forward slash, a drive letter, or a file extension is mapped to <filepath> rather than <codeph>. Similarly, a sequence of bold UI labels separated by > is mapped to <menucascade><uicontrol>.
